title: Apertus 1.5 Release Notes
gist: Swiss AI's Apertus 1.5 extends its fully open 8B and 70B models with early-fusion image and audio understanding, an optional thinking mode and a 262k-token context window under Apache 2.0. It still trails frontier open-weight models but is competitive on some tasks, and the team announced an Apertus 2.0 roadmap with a roughly 600B-parameter sparse/MoE model.

insights.claim: Apertus 1.5 adds image and audio understanding, an optional thinking mode, a 262,144-token context window (4x Apertus 1.0), better instruction-following and tool use to the 8B and 70B models, with weights released July 24, 2026 under Apache 2.0.
insights.speaker: Hanna Yukhymenko
insights.so_what: A fully open, permissively licensed European model family is closing capability gaps, relevant for sovereign-AI procurement.

insights.claim: Apertus 1.5 is a continued pretraining of Apertus 1.0 adding 4T tokens to the 8B model and 2T to the 70B (totals 19T and 17T), and the models are fully open with open weights, open data, open values and full training details.
insights.speaker: Hanna Yukhymenko
insights.so_what: Full-stack openness (data and recipes) differentiates Apertus from open-weight-only releases and supports reproducibility.

insights.claim: All Apertus training data, including the new multimodal data, is publicly available, permissively licensed and respects robots.txt opt-outs retroactively, with every source listed in apertus-data-transparency.
insights.speaker: Hanna Yukhymenko
insights.so_what: A compliance-oriented data policy lowers copyright and regulatory risk for enterprise adopters in the EU.

insights.claim: Apertus 1.5 uses early-fusion multimodality where images (Emu3.5 tokenizer, 1,024 tokens for a 512x512 image) and audio (WavTokenizer, 40 tokens per second) enter as discrete tokens in the same sequence as text, extending only the vocabulary so the architecture is unchanged and training runs at text-only speed; the models understand images and audio but generate only text.
insights.speaker: Hanna Yukhymenko
insights.so_what: Tokenizer-based multimodality avoids separate vision encoders and training-speed penalties, a cost-efficient route for open labs.

insights.claim: Pretraining proceeds in four stages (unpaired, paired, cooldown with more math and code, long context from 8k to 262k), with more than half of tokens text-only to preserve the language abilities of Apertus 1.0, and refreshed text sources such as FineWeb2-HQ+, FinePDFs and Nemotron-CC.
insights.speaker: Hanna Yukhymenko
insights.so_what: A reference recipe for adding modalities to a text model without regressing text ability.
insights.locator: Starting from Apertus 1.0, we continue pretraining in four stages

insights.claim: Post-training runs SFT, long-context SFT, RL with verifiable rewards (about 350k prompts), DPO and charter alignment (SDPO), with reasoning traces added only to prompts the model cannot already solve and tool-use data restricted to execution-verified trajectories.
insights.speaker: Hanna Yukhymenko
insights.so_what: Targeted reasoning data and verified tool trajectories are practical data-efficiency tactics.

insights.claim: Long-context SFT at the full 262k window is needed to restore the long-context ability that short-context SFT erodes.
insights.speaker: Hanna Yukhymenko
insights.so_what: Post-training order matters for long-context retention; relevant for teams fine-tuning open models.
insights.locator: Long-context SFT at the full 262k window

insights.claim: Mixing multimodal data with text during SFT improves performance across all modalities, and the benefits of multimodal reasoning traces survive subsequent text-only RL, which improves mathematics more when starting from a checkpoint trained with multimodal traces.
insights.speaker: Hanna Yukhymenko
insights.so_what: Supports multimodal training even for text-reasoning gains.

insights.claim: Apertus 1.5 still trails frontier open-weight models but improved significantly in coding and instruction following, with the 8B outperforming similarly sized open-weight models on instruction-following and multilingual tasks, and thinking mode improving results on reasoning-heavy benchmarks like AIME.
insights.speaker: Hanna Yukhymenko
insights.so_what: Competitive at small scale but not frontier; adoption depends on openness and sovereignty rather than raw capability.
insights.quote: While still trailing frontier open-weight models

insights.claim: Apertus 1.5 multimodal performance is closer to Gemma 4 12B and other current open-weight models, competitive in spatial understanding among open-weight models and in document/chart understanding among open-source models.
insights.speaker: Hanna Yukhymenko
insights.so_what: Multimodal parity with mid-size open models is achieved with fully open data.
insights.locator: The multimodal performance of the model is closer to Gemma 4 12B

insights.claim: On the Last Translation Benchmark, Apertus 1.5 8B matches GPT-OSS-20B in machine translation and outperforms Claude Haiku 4.5 and Google Translate, and it performs on par with leading open-weight models on Swiss Legal tasks.
insights.speaker: Hanna Yukhymenko
insights.so_what: Small open multilingual models can rival commercial translation, a threat to niche translation services; results are self-reported.

insights.claim: Apertus publishes results in the Every Eval Ever (EEE) schema with the EvalEval Coalition, recording who ran the evaluation, model access, generation settings and metric interpretation; EvalEval found the schema can represent 56 of the 60 evaluation-reporting elements demanded by frameworks including EU AI Act Article 55 and the GPAI Code of Practice.
insights.speaker: Hanna Yukhymenko
insights.so_what: Machine-readable eval reporting may become a compliance standard for AI developers in the EU.

insights.claim: Apertus publishes a Public Summary of Training Content and voluntarily a Code of Practice document alongside the models, positioning it as ahead of regulatory expectations.
insights.speaker: Hanna Yukhymenko
insights.so_what: Early compliance documentation can ease European enterprise and public-sector adoption.
insights.locator: This fits how we already release Apertus

insights.claim: Proton Lumo and Infomaniak Euria have integrated Apertus 1.5, and API access has been announced by Swisscom, Infomaniak, Phoeniqs and others.
insights.speaker: Hanna Yukhymenko
insights.so_what: Swiss and European privacy-focused providers are building on sovereign open models.

insights.claim: Apertus has passed five million downloads on Hugging Face, and the team announced a roadmap for Apertus 2.0 at the AI+X Summit in Zurich: a sparse/MoE architecture of about 600B total parameters, extended training schedule, prioritizing agents, mathematics and coding.
insights.speaker: Hanna Yukhymenko
insights.so_what: A roughly 8x jump in parameters signals a push toward frontier-class open models from Europe.
